# Generation 8 charter — Mode B, open relational exploration

Generation 8 is the first execution of Mode B. The inquiry note is `constraint-lab/docs/inquiry-modes.md`. Generations 1 through 7B stay Mode A evidence. Their files are not rewritten.

## Question

What happens when higher-order relational context participates in an evolving stochastic relational system, and which recurrent structures, routes, transformations, and context dependencies appear?

A completed trajectory has no scientific pass or fail. Unexpected behaviour is an observation.

## What the runtime contains

The process contains only:

```text
state
possible events
constraint weights
stochastic event selection
```

Derived records may later describe organisation, persistence, dissolution, reorganisation, return, recurrence, routing, context dependence, repair-like return, or boundary-like persistence. Those words are not rewards, targets, or semantic goals. The engine does not seek a destination class.

The unconstrained system is baseline relational dynamics. This charter does not call it a null hypothesis.

Exploration choices are made between rounds, after observations. No trajectory is trained or scored so that a larger divergence, entropy, or residence becomes a reward.

## Fixed ontology

```text
N = 4
O = 3
G = 0
S = 0
H = 0
L = 0
independent hypergraph
```

The state is 6 pair bits and 4 independent triad bits: 10 bits, 1024 full states. Geometry, explicit memory, entity state, meta-constraints, simplicial face closure, and a larger N are outside this generation.

## Clocks

The full-event clock counts every toggle, including triad-only events. The pair-event epoch counts toggles of the six pair slots. Routing summaries may use the pair-event epoch. Triad-only timing stays in the event stream.

## Rounds

At most four rounds:

```text
Round 0
Round 1
Round 2
Round 3
```

Round 0 is a starter atlas:

```text
baseline
the canonical structural T->P singleton archetypes from Generation 4, at strong_suppress
one Generation 5 disjoint-action T->P + P->P anchor, both rules at strong_suppress
```

`prohibit` is absent from Round 0 so the first atlas keeps finite stochastic support. A later round may introduce `prohibit` only when an observation gives a concrete reason to inspect a hard-support boundary, written in the journey before that round runs.

Adaptive rounds contain at most four new systems. Extra seeds, a narrower context scope, or a different finite grade on a system already run counts as one of the four when it adds substantive compute. The default replicate count is 16. A later round may use 32 or 64 on a narrower set when the journey says the allocation is for trajectory resolution. That is not a power calculation and it is not a significance test.

Allowed perturbation operators, unless a committed plan amends the list:

```text
weight_shift among strong_suppress, weak_suppress, weak_favour, strong_favour
condition_polarity_flip present <-> absent
structural_tp_neighbour among the known canonical T->P orbits
add_pp_companion from the Generation 4 P->P canonical set, total rules at most 2
remove_rule from a two-rule system
```

Ontology axes stay fixed. Adaptive rounds ordinarily reuse the Round 0 source and context-orbit basis. A narrower scope keeps the Round 0 context ids and says why.

## Frozen plans

Every round executes only after its plan commit exists on the remote. The plan hash covers the palette, the horizon, the seed schedule, the context basis, the replicate count, and the work count. The commit SHA is `frozen_exploration_plan_commit`. The plan file does not contain that SHA. The runner refuses to start without a 40-hex commit whose committed plan hash matches the plan being executed. Result artifacts record the SHA. Scientific results are a later commit.

## Horizon preflight

The primary horizon is 512 pair-event epochs, with a safety cap of 16,384 full events. Before Round 0, a cost benchmark may reduce the horizon. The reduction rule is operational and is applied before any atlas is interpreted:

```text
If the estimated Round 0 wall at 2 workers exceeds 3 hours,
or the estimated compressed event storage exceeds 2 GiB,
or one replay exceeds 5 seconds,
freeze 256 pair events instead of 512.
If that reduced horizon still exceeds either budget, freeze 128.
If 128 still exceeds either budget, stop and record the estimate.
Do not read route outcomes in order to choose the horizon.
```

Termination reasons `pair_horizon`, `full_event_cap`, and `no_admissible_event` are observations. The episode record remains valid.

## Attention

When a later round is chosen, each candidate carries an unsummed attention vector. The coordinates are ordinal 0–5:

```text
CN contextual novelty
RD routing diversity
RC recurrence / return structure
EC explanatory-compression potential
CG coherence relevance
CB computational boundedness
```

The coordinates are not a confidence score and not a pass/fail score. They are not added together.

## Interpretation boundary

Simulation, observation, and structural inference may contribute to a coherence assessment. They do not establish a Designer, a Christian ontology, or an ultimate receiver. Those remain upstream or broader premises.

Each round report separates observations, inferences, the coherence reading, and the next options. Causal wording stays out of the observation tables.

## Journey

`journey.jsonl` is append-only. A decision record is not rewritten after it is written.

# Generation 8 event schema

Schema id: `rs-constraint-lab.generation-008-event/v1`

The event stream is the primary scientific object. Derived tables are summaries of that stream. A seed by itself is not the forensic record.

## Clocks and draw

Selection reuses the laboratory toggle kernel. Baseline weight is 1 on every relation slot. A matching constraint multiplies that weight by its alphabet factor. Round 0 uses alphabet `W4`. `strong_suppress` is `1/4`.

The draw is one call to Python `random.Random.randrange(norm)` on MT19937. `norm` is the sum of the integer weights after the least common multiple of the fraction denominators. The stored uniform draw is the unreduced rational `draw/norm`. That is a discrete uniform integer on `0 .. norm-1`. It is not a binary floating-point sample.

A pair slot is one of the first six relation slots. A triad slot is one of the last four. `pair_index` is null on a triad-only event. Those events remain in the stream.

## Episode header

Each episode record stores:

```text
episode_id
experiment_id
round_id
system_id
source_graph_class
hidden_context_orbit_id
replicate_index
seed
seed_function
initial_state
initial_state_hash
final_state
final_state_hash
constraint_system_hash
event_stream_sha256
event_payload_sha256
trajectory_hash
spec_hash
frozen_plan_commit
runner_version
python_version
termination_reason
event_count
pair_event_count
```

`trajectory_hash` is the rolling SHA-256. It starts from the canonical initial-state record and folds each canonical event line.

`event_payload_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the uncompressed canonical JSONL bytes. `event_stream_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the gzip file that stores those bytes. Replay checks the payload hash, the rolling hash, the recomputed weights, and the draw.

## Event fields

One JSON object per line, canonical key order when hashed:

```text
t
pre
post
slot
kind
pair_index
full_index
draw
norm
uniform_draw
selected_weight
selected_integer
probability
weight_hash
weights
rules
pair_before
pair_after
triad_before
triad_after
context_before
context_after
rng_token
```

`weights` is the ten fraction strings, one per slot, before normalisation. `weight_hash` is their SHA-256. `rules` lists the indexes of constraints whose `matches` predicate accepted the selected slot. `kind` is `form` or `dissolve`. `rng_token` is `sha256-u64-v1:<draws consumed before this event>`. Restoring the seed and consuming `randrange` that many times restores the generator. Segment cursors also store `random.Random.getstate()` so a resumed segment does not recompute earlier events.

`pair_before` and `pair_after` are indexes into the eleven-name class table stored on the episode header. `context_before` and `context_after` name the triad-configuration orbit under the automorphism group of the current labelled pair graph. The label is `p{pair_mask:02d}-t{canonical_triad:02d}-s{orbit_size}`. `canonical_triad` is the least triad index in that orbit. The raw full state remains the ground truth.

## Storage

```text
episodes/<episode_id>.json          header and derived summary
streams/<episode_id>.jsonl.gz       canonical event JSONL, gzip
```

`trajectory inspect <episode-id>` prints the events with class names. Replay of a valid episode reports `verification = exact`.

## Segment chain

If a segment boundary is used, the next segment receives the previous final state, the RNG state, the event counts, and the rolling trajectory hash. The chained stream is required to match a one-process execution of the same episode. `segment_boundary` is an execution cursor. It is not a scientific termination reason.

## Derived summaries

Summaries are computed from the event stream. Route labels are recomputed from the run-length encoding of the pair-class sequence. A cached route string is not an input to that calculation.

The pair-class sequence includes epoch 0, the initial state. Each pair event appends the post-event class. Run lengths sum to `pair_event_count + 1`. The 11×11 transition matrix counts pair events, including events that stay inside a class. Its total is `pair_event_count`.

Route motifs of length 2, 3, and 4 are counted on the change-compressed class path. That path collapses consecutive events that stay inside one isomorphism class. The transition matrix keeps those stays. The atlas records how many motif keys were omitted above the retained 60.

# Generation 008A charter

Generation 8A is Mode B, open relational exploration. A completed trajectory has no scientific pass or fail. The scientific object is the fully replayable stochastic trajectory.

The repair is sampling, not a new dynamical law. For each visible source graph the execution basis is all 16 raw triad configurations. Symmetry is computed afterwards. `Aut(source graph, constraint system)` is the set of vertex permutations that preserve both the labelled source pair graph and the labelled constraint multiset. That subgroup may describe equivalence among starts. It does not delete a start from the plan.

Generation 8 graph-only orbit labels remain historical. They are analysis metadata on a Generation 8A episode, not seed coordinates.

Ontology, unchanged: N=4, O=3, G=S=H=L=0, independent hypergraph.

Round A0 is the repair palette copied from the committed Generation 8 plans. Later rounds, if opened, are chosen after A0 observations and are frozen before they run. The generation may stop before A2.

# Generation 008C charter

The question is a mechanism reading of structures already measured in Generations 8, 8A, and 8B:

```text
How does a higher-order triadic condition alter the local lower-order event law, how does visible graph topology convert that local event bias into edge-count versus shape changes, and why is the influence of the initial triadic context rapidly forgotten?
```

The aim is explanatory compression. A higher-order effect that is locally genuine, and an initial-condition footprint that is small and short-lived, should be read from the same exact transition geometry.

Ontology, unchanged: N=4, O=3, G=S=H=L=0, independent hypergraph, alphabet W4.

Round C0 is the only frozen analysis round. It uses exact constraint semantics, exact pair-slot weights, the exact pair-event epoch kernel, exact graph classification, and exact finite-state enumeration. A later round is not defined until C0 has been read.

Graph classes are descriptors of pairwise relation sets. Organisation, repair, routing success, boundary, and preferred graph are not targets and are not scores.

Pass and fail remain appropriate for software, CI, validation, and execution contracts. They are not the vocabulary of the mechanism reading.

The three epistemic layers stay separate: observation, inference, and RS / global-coherence interpretation.

# Generation 008E charter

Generation 8E is Mode B, open relational exploration. It does not introduce history or meta-constraints. It does not enlarge N. It runs no stochastic trajectory census, fits no parameter, and adds no control family.

The question is:

```text
What genuinely new local relational structure appears when one ordinary constraint can read two higher-order relations conjunctively?
```

Generation 8D exhausted compositions of two primitive one-condition rules (rule cardinality 2, each rule K=2) and found no gate×gate logit coefficient in that subgrammar. Generation 8E holds rule cardinality at 1 and raises expression complexity to K=3: one pair action conditioned on two distinct triad literals, with one finite weight. The two axes are kept separate. Neither is ranked on one scalar.

## Why K before L

The ordinary `Constraint` grammar already accepts several conjunctive conditions in one rule. Before any change to the ontology, such as meta-constraints (`L > 0`) or history (`H > 0`), the round asks what the existing grammar can already express. K controls simultaneous expression complexity. H controls dependence on prior states. L controls constraints on constraints. None of them is used to obtain what another already supplies.

## Scope

- Ontology, unchanged: N=4, O=3, G=S=H=L=0, independent hypergraph.
- The primary family is every single K=3 rule with a pair action and two distinct triad literals, at the four W4 grades.
- Round E0 is the complete local census of that family, together with small algebraic items: the K2-versus-K3 symbolic comparison, the Boolean (Möbius) and corner bases, and targeted XOR and XNOR constructions from two K3 rules. It is frozen before it is executed.
- E1 is optional. It is opened only if E0 leaves a genuine global question, and it is frozen before execution.

## Discipline

Observations, inferences and the RS / global-coherence interpretation stay in separate layers. Magnitude, robustness, persistence, explanatory reach and structural role stay separate. No system is ranked by a scalar. Pass and fail are reserved for software, CI, validation and execution contracts.

# Constraint grammar

## 1. State and event space

For N labelled entities, O=2 contains one bit for each unordered pair; O=3 appends one bit for each unordered triad. Slots are lexicographic pairs followed by lexicographic triads. At N=4, D=6+4=10 and there are 1024 full states. Independent hypergraph means no simplicial face-closure condition, not statistical independence of event histories.

A baseline event toggles exactly one relation bit. There is one candidate event per slot in every state, interpreted as form if absent and dissolve if present. O>3 is not implemented. Fixed current-state semantics here have G=S=H=L=0.

## 2. Constraint syntax

In the literal fragment:

```text
direction ::= form | dissolve
literal   ::= present(relation) | absent(relation)
rule      ::= direction(action_relation) [| literal (& literal)*] => factor_name
collection ::= rule occurrences
```

Both pair and triad actions and conditions are accepted at O=3. Conditions may name any other relation slot, but not the action itself. Direction already tests the action bit. Literal ordering is canonicalised. Identical repeated literals are rejected; contradictory literals on the same relation are accepted and never match.

The full O=2 DSL also admits a single count predicate (count >=, <= or == threshold). The O=3 parser rejects count predicates. Parser tokens name factors; the kernel looks their values up in a factor map. The standard experiment specification restricts factor names to its finite alphabet, whereas the parser itself does not.

## 3. Weight semantics

Let \(\phi_i(x,e)\) be 1 exactly when event, direction guard and all conditions of rule i match. With the implemented slot-constant baseline weights \(b_e>0\) and positive multipliers:

\[
w(e\mid x,\mathcal C)=b_e\prod_{i=1}^J m_i^{\phi_i(x,e)}.
\]

The unnormalised full-event law is divided by the sum over all D candidate slots. All integrated single-action formulas take baseline weights to be 1.

Zero prohibit is supported elsewhere in the DSL but excluded from positive-log algebra, full-support irreducibility and expressivity theorems. If all event weights vanish, the implementation records deadlock and completes the Markov kernel with a self-loop; that completion is not a relational event.

## 4. Logit representation

\[
\ell_e(x)=\log b_e+\sum_i \lambda_i\phi_i(x,e),\qquad \lambda_i=\log m_i.
\]

This additive expression is a model-level meaning of 'constraints as language': syntax selects features, semantics assigns log weights, composition sums features, and interpretation produces transitions. Probabilities are not additive because normalisation couples all event slots.

Full q equality permits a common state-dependent weight scale. In the one-action analyses the other slots are fixed to unit weights, removing that gauge ambiguity.

## 5. Expression complexity

The implemented count is K=1+number of literal tokens+number of count predicates. A non-neutral, satisfiable conjunction of r distinct raw Boolean gates contributes degree r, with K=r+1 in the literal fragment. Syntactic K does not guarantee degree: contradictions vanish, cancellations can remove top coefficients, and count predicates may read several bits with one token.

## 6. Rule cardinality

J counts simultaneous occurrences. Multiplication is commutative, but it is not idempotent: repeating a matching rule squares its multiplier. The backend accepts repeated occurrences. Historical primary censuses use distinct labelled sets with a structurally simple normal form excluding repeated action/condition identity even at different grades.

Increasing J at fixed primitive feature family sums more terms from that family. It cannot create a new log-weight monomial outside the family's span. It can still cause nonlinear probability and global observable effects.

## 7. Boolean feature hierarchy

Every real table on r Boolean gates has a unique multilinear expansion. Conjunction monomials of degrees 0 through r supply a basis; complete literal corners supply another. Increasing maximum K makes higher-degree individual features available, subject to parser scope and alphabet. See [derivations](derivations.md).

This is local log-weight expressivity, not arbitrary transition-support universality.

## 8. Equivalence notions

Canonical syntax, weight tables, normalised event laws, full kernels, conjugate kernels and declared projected processes are different objects. Aggregate statistic equality is weaker still. [Equivalences](equivalences.md) states the hierarchy and its clock/initial-prior requirements.

## 9. Symmetry

Vertex permutations relabel both states and rules. For a fixed labelled rule collection, only actual kernel automorphisms are symmetry quotients. Independent hidden-bit permutations can preserve a law while failing to preserve vertex incidence. Visible graph isomorphism alone need not define a Markov quotient.

## 10. Local-to-global pipeline

Syntax -> active features -> event log weights -> normalised probabilities -> kernel -> clocked dynamics -> state distribution -> projection -> statistic.

No topology creates a missing local log-weight monomial. Normalisation and dynamics can nevertheless transform how it becomes observable. The mechanism audit is in [local-to-global](local-to-global.md).

## 11. Projection hierarchy

Labelled pair mask -> graph isomorphism class -> edge count are nested deterministic projections. Their law-label information has an exact chain decomposition. Projection can erase distinctions and need not preserve Markov structure.

## 12. Memory versus current efficacy

A current hidden gate can affect the next event even when its initial value is no longer discriminable in a later visible graph. Hidden current-state dependence is not H>0. Full-event and next-pair-event clocks must be distinguished.

## 13. Boundaries of current-state grammar

The unbounded literal parser plus arbitrary positive factor map can construct every positive event-weight table on its fixed single-bit-toggle support, using direction to encode the action bit and conditions for all other bits. The bounded experiment runner cannot be silently identified with this larger representation core.

This gives neither arbitrary transition support nor different futures for identical complete current states under one fixed rule collection. Finite W4 coverage is separate from continuous algebraic completeness.

## 14. Open axes H and L

H asks for dependence on different histories ending at the same complete current material state. L asks for dynamical constraint-state configurations under a common program, not merely two different static rule sets. Either may become ordinary Markov state after augmentation; such augmentation changes the representation and must preserve the declared clock/support if claimed equivalent.

## 15. Scope and non-claims

All theorems specify finite state space, positive factors, feature fragment and clock. Numerical results retain their original domain and tolerance. There is no claim of physical spacetime emergence, ultimate receiver, design, theology, or nature implementing this DSL. Book changes are deferred to explicit later work.

# Derivations and scope All results in this document concern the literal, fixed-current-state model with positive multipliers unless stated otherwise. They are not proofs about the RS ontology or physical reality. The canonical catalogue states assumptions and historical evidence separately. ## CL-T01 and CL-T02: composition and order The kernel loops over matching rules and multiplies each factor into the baseline slot weight. Thus \(w_e=b_e\prod_i m_i^{\phi_i}\) and \(\ell_e=\log b_e+\sum_i(\log m_i)\phi_i\). Finite products commute, as do the sums. Exact rational evaluation is order independent. Floating-point summation can have roundoff-order differences. Canonicalisation sorts rule representations and minimises their joint vertex images; it does not make multiplication idempotent. Duplicate backend occurrences contribute repeatedly. The structurally simple census normal form excludes repeated structural identity. Alphabet labels and factor values must be included when interpreting syntax. ## CL-T03: the six-slot law With six pair slots, one admissible slot has weight m and the other five have weight 1. Conditioning the next full event to be a pair event gives \(q_m(e_*)=m/(m+5)\) and \(q_m(e)=1/(m+5)\) otherwise. Inactive m=1 gives 1/6 each. This is not the next-pair epoch resolvent: hidden events may occur before that epoch. ## CL-T04: complementary gate elimination For a binary gate g, exactly one of g and 1-g is active. Two same-action, same-direction rules at multiplier m give \(m^g m^{1-g}=m\) whenever the action is admissible. When inadmissible, both rules fail their direction guard. All event weights agree with an unconditional rule of that direction, hence full kernels agree as well. ## CL-T05: direction elimination Equal factors on form(e_*)|g and dissolve(e_*)|g give weight \(m^g\) for the slot irrespective of its current bit. Exactly one direction is admissible. Dependence on g remains, and normalised probabilities remain coupled to the denominator. This does not eliminate the event's form/dissolve interpretation. ## CL-T06: one-literal additive bound Fix one admissible action direction and two raw gate bits. Every one-literal rule contributes either \(\lambda g_i\) or \(\lambda(1-g_i)\); unconditional rules contribute constants. Summing gives \(\ell=c+a g_1+b g_2\), so \(\Delta_{12}\ell=0\). This is a bound on log weights in a fixed feature family, not on normalised probabilities, full-state action guards, count predicates, or higher-K conjunctions. ## CL-T07 and CL-T08: conjunction degree Let U_i=g_i for a present literal and U_i=1-g_i for an absent literal. A rule on r distinct gates contributes \(\lambda\prod_i U_i\) on its admissible action. The coefficient of \(\prod_i g_i\) is \(\lambda(-1)^{n_{\mathrm{absent}}}\), which is nonzero when m!=1. In literal coordinates its top discrete derivative is \(\lambda\). For r=2, \(\ell_{11}-\ell_{10}-\ell_{01}+\ell_{00}=\log m\) in literal coordinates. The raw-bit sign is positive for zero or two absent literals and negative for one. Distinct gates guarantee each full corner assignment is possible in the independent hypergraph. Contradictory literals on the same gate have zero feature. Repetition can reduce degree (g*g=g). The parser rejects identical repeats but accepts present(g)&absent(g). Neutral factors and cancellation among rules can also remove top interaction. The theorem concerns one non-neutral, satisfiable rule, not syntactic condition count alone. ## CL-T09: Boolean/Mobius basis For a table f on \(\{0,1\}^r\), write 1_B for the corner with precisely B active. Set \[ \theta_B=\sum_{C\subseteq B}(-1)^{|B|-|C|}f(1_C). \] Then \(f(g)=\sum_{B\subseteq[r]}\theta_B\prod_{i\in B}g_i\). At corner 1_D, exchanging subset sums leaves f(1_D): the inner alternating sum vanishes unless C=D. The triangular corner-to-coefficient transform has diagonal 1, proving uniqueness. The empty product is 1. ## CL-T10 and CL-T11: corner basis and one-action expressivity Corner indicators \(\chi_u(g)=\prod_i[g_i=u_i]\) are mutually exclusive and sum to 1. Thus \(f=\sum_u f(u)\chi_u\). Expanding the absent literals gives the Mobius transformation; evaluation on corners gives its inverse. For any strictly positive desired action-weight table w(u), assign multiplier w(u)/b to the complete corner rule u. Exactly one rule matches on an admissible action. # Equivalence, symmetry and quotienting

## Declared hierarchy

| Notion | Required agreement | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical syntax | Same canonical rule collection and factor interpretation | Vertex-relabelling canonicalisation is declared; duplicate multiplicity is not erased |
| Unnormalised law | Same event weights at every full current state | Sufficient but not necessary for q equality |
| Local full-event law | Same normalised event distribution at every state | Positive weights may differ by a common state-dependent scale |
| Full-kernel equality | Same P on the same labelled state space | Equivalent to full-event law equality here because each toggle has a distinct successor |
| Conjugacy | P'(f(x),f(x'))=P(x,x') for an explicit bijection f | Initial distributions and event projections must map too |
| Projected process equality | Same declared projected finite-dimensional distributions | Specify clock, initial prior, projection and horizon family; projection need not be Markov |
| Statistic equality | Same chosen occupancy, passage or information statistic | Strictly weaker than process equality |

Immediate pair-conditioned slot equality is not full-event equality: multiplying every pair weight by 2 preserves conditional pair probabilities but changes pair-versus-hidden-event hazard. Nor does it automatically preserve the next-pair epoch kernel.

Generation 7B's fitted aggregate collapse is not a proof of projected-process equivalence. Once its equal complementary factors are specified, CL-T04 proves equality to an unconditional local/full kernel, which is a different claim. Generation 8D provides several full-state eliminations and distinct law-coordinate patterns. Generation 8F provides explicit hidden-state conjugacies fixing visible pair labels.

## Vertex covariance versus automorphism

A vertex permutation maps both relation coordinates and rules. This covariance is available to the labelled model. Keeping rules fixed generally leaves only a stabiliser subgroup as automorphisms. Quotienting by all S4 graph isomorphisms while ignoring a labelled law can destroy transition semantics; 8A repaired exactly that error.

For partition blocks, strong lumpability requires equal total transition probability from any two states in one block into every destination block. Automorphism orbit partitions satisfy this condition. Isomorphic visible pair graphs with different raw hidden configurations need not.

## Independent hidden-bit symmetries

At N=4 the four independent hidden triad bits have symmetric baseline flips. A coordinate permutation need not arise from a vertex permutation to conjugate a selected one-action law. Complement maps can also work when literal polarity and priors map.

The BOTH/ONE/NEITHER placements are structurally distinct under S4 but dynamically conjugate in the 8F grammar, with pair projection fixed. This is exact projected-process equality for mapped uniform-hidden priors, not an assertion that all triad-conditioned kernels are exchangeable.

## Incidence boundary

Independent hypergraph state coordinates do not automatically impose face coupling. 'Pair is a face of triad' is metadata until used by the law. Independence of coordinates does not imply statistical independence of paths: normalisation couples slot probabilities.

Incidence can become dynamically consequential within an existing ordinary grammar by choosing correlated face-action templates, several coupled pair actions, or pair-dependent gate behaviour. Alternatives include simplicial closure, geometry or shared-state coupling, but no such extension is selected in 8G. L or H is not required merely to consult incidence when constructing fixed rules.

# Expressivity boundaries

## Four distinct representation layers

1. **Backend semantics:** fixed occurrences multiply factors; duplicates have multiplicity.
2. **Literal parser core:** O=2/O=3, any supported action slot, both directions and conjunctions over all other supported relation bits; no intrinsic K ceiling; custom factor names accepted.
3. **Normal form:** historical primary censuses require structurally simple sets; stacked-weight comparisons are separate.
4. **Experiment runner:** W4/W3/W16 named alphabets and J in {1,2,3}, plus frozen cell-specific K/A limits.

A theorem about layer 2 with unbounded positive parameters is not a theorem that layer 4 has already enumerated or can request that entire family.

## Current-state expressivity: proved with restrictions

[CL-T12](derivations.md#cl-t12) gives a constructive proof of all strictly positive current-state event-weight functions on the existing finite single-toggle support. Direction encodes the action bit; a full conjunction encodes every other bit. The upper bound is K<=D, J<=D*2^D. This is not a new census and does not require a G0 computation.

A desired positive kernel with that support can use its probabilities as weights. Kernels with multibit transitions, extra states or self-loops are outside this support theorem. Arbitrary history dependence is outside a fixed current-state representation. Rational parameters are exact in the backend; arbitrary reals are the algebraic idealisation, and irrational numerical references require precision/error reporting.

## K, J and interaction

One action plus r distinct satisfiable literals has K=r+1 and nonzero top gate coefficient if non-neutral. A sum of features cannot manufacture a missing monomial in log weights. It can manufacture non-additive probability or observable effects through normalisation.

A count predicate is a compound feature, not one Boolean gate. The explicit count>=1 counterexample has K=2 and degree 2 over two remaining pair bits. Therefore the formal K/order hierarchy is **literal-only**, not a blanket theorem about every token in the DSL. Historical claims remain visible and receive a scope relation.

## Continuous parameters versus finite W4

Continuous completeness follows from either corner or monomial bases. W4 coefficients lie on a log-base-2 integer lattice. Non-dyadic multipliers are impossible using finite positive W4 products. Structural simplicity additionally bounds how many features can stack at a corner.

[CL-T21](derivations.md#cl-t21) proves selected minimal [J,max-K] vectors without enumeration. It distinguishes constant 8 as continuous [1,1], structurally simple W4 [3,2], and stacked W4 [2,1]. A constant 3 is not a W4 product at any finite J. The earlier 625-table basis grids are narrower than the whole structurally simple family.

Minimum J and minimum maximum-K are separate optimisation coordinates. General targets can have tradeoffs; these selected examples attain both stated minima jointly. The empty baseline's [0,0] is a bookkeeping convention, not a claim that K=0 is a new primitive rule.

## What H adds

Let x contain **all** ordinary material relation bits, including hidden triads. A fixed ordinary collection assigns one future row to x. If two reachable histories end at the same x yet a common controller assigns distinct future distributions, no increase of K or J at unchanged x can reproduce both rows.

Finite history can often be encoded in an augmented Markov state. That is a representation change, not compilation into the same ordinary state. Preserving the exact event support and event clock may require additional update semantics; do not silently insert stuttering or multibit updates.

## What L adds

A dynamical constraint state eta can change coefficients, polarity, existence, scope or rule interpretation under a common program. Two separately chosen static constraint sets already give different kernels at L=0 and are not an L witness.

If eta is a function of ordinary x and the resulting law has existing positive support, CL-T12 compiles it into a larger fixed ordinary grammar (continuous/unbounded budgets). If independent reachable eta values give different futures at identical x, extra represented state is needed. This proves a state-boundary issue, not automatic irreducibility of every meta syntax.

## Permanent compilation test

Before introducing an axis, specify:
- represented state and what counts as identical current state;
- event/update support and clock;
- visible projection, initial priors and demanded process equivalence;
- alphabet and allowed K/J budget;
- whether compilation may augment state.

Then either provide a construction and representation tradeoff, or an exact non-compilability witness. Aggregate fit, larger CMI or a novel syntax name is insufficient. Hard zero support requires a separate extension of the positive theorem.

## Pipeline

~~~mermaid
flowchart TD
  SY["Constraint syntax"] --> FV["Active feature vector"]
  FV --> LG["Unnormalised event log weights"]
  LG --> Q["Normalised event probabilities"]
  Q --> P["Full transition kernel"]

~~~

| Arrow | What is specified or lost | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Syntax -> features | Satisfiability, direction and gate placement; neutral/redundant syntax may collapse | Boolean evaluation |
| Features -> log weights | Coefficients compose; different feature decompositions can yield the same function | Linear sum |
| Log weights -> probabilities | Common statewise shifts disappear; all slots become coupled | Exponentiation and shared denominator |
| Probabilities -> kernel | Event support and successor map are fixed; event labels can be lost if successors coincide | State update; injective toggles here |
| Kernel -> clocked dynamics | Hidden-only excursions are integrated out in E, not in immediate pair conditioning | Resolvent, products and path sums |
| Dynamics -> distribution | Initial priors/time horizon matter; stationarity removes source information but periodic limits need parity | Linear propagation; spectral/balance structure |
| Distribution -> projection | Labels, raw hidden coordinates or graph shape can be erased; a quotient need not be Markov | Deterministic many-to-one map |
| Projection -> statistic | Chosen summaries discard distinctions; equal statistics do not prove process equivalence | Information, passage or occupancy functional |

No downstream operation can reconstruct a distinction already erased without additional information. Nonlinear operations can redistribute existing distinctions among observables; they do not create a missing primitive gate coefficient in the original log-weight function.

## Normalisation is distinct from feature interaction

R05's denominator effect and 8D's probability-level interaction coexist with additive logits. In 8F, PROJECTION removes constant and first-order log-weight components under **uniform corners**, not under nonlinear probability or stationary weighting. Thus a centered interaction can still alter mean probability and occupancy.

ENDPOINT fixes two corners, PROJECTION fixes lower-order log components, and DRIFT fixes one balanced probability moment. None universally dominates; retain separate comparison vectors.

## Topology routes visibility

The same affected slot has different shape consequences in different visible graphs. In the canonical path, dissolving the middle edge and an end edge produces different unlabelled two-edge shapes. Formation when the action is already present is initially inadmissible. Star/triangle sources and their labelled action positions differ.

8C and 8F show this routing at committed finite horizons; they do not prove the path always dominates. 8F explicitly records path-not-universal. Edge count, shape conditional on edges, and labels conditional on class remain separate channels.

## Nested projection information

For mask X, class Y and edge count Z, CL-T16 gives
I(M;X)=I(M;Z)+I(M;Y|Z)+I(M;X|Y).
Each term answers a different question. Equal-prior JS measures law discrimination, not a scalar global interaction strength. Graph-class projection is finer than edge count, coarser than labelled mask.

## Clocks and current information

P takes one full toggle. Immediate pair q conditions the current slot law on a pair event. E waits through arbitrarily many hidden-only toggles before the next pair arrival. Pair-event stationary arrival occupancy differs from full-event occupancy and from event-weighted pre-pair context.

A current triad can predict the next pair slot even when the initial triad is forgotten in visible state. Current CMI is not historical memory. The 8F suppression case has lower stationary current CMI but greater K3/PROJECTION pair JS than favouring; no monotone prediction law follows.

## Stationary mechanism and limits

CL-T18 proves action-bit occupancy times uniform other pairs when action rates depend only on action and hidden bits. CL-T19 then proves stationary shape-given-edge invariance. The numerical 8F factorisation gap (~2.6e-15) verifies that palette; the new general proof is a distinct formal result with stricter stated assumptions.

At stationarity tiny edge and labelled residues can remain while shape disappears. At even checkpoints a fixed-parity source approaches a parity-conditioned stationary vector, not full stationary occupancy. Source forgetting does not erase all model discrimination.

## Evidential vector

Magnitude, robustness, temporal character, structural role, projection sensitivity and epistemic layer are not summed. The tiny 8F PROJECTION residue is persistent within tolerance, structurally diagnostic of a centered interaction comparison, and projection-dependent. Its size does not prove ontological importance. Conversely a large ENDPOINT difference may reflect unmatched lower-order bias.

Finite-model observations, mechanism inferences and RS/global-coherence interpretations must remain separate. The formal system explains model behaviour without establishing physical spacetime, receiver, design or theology.
